descriptions.title: Subscription-first, not algorithm-first
descriptions.body: TubeScout's whole premise is that you already curated your channels by subscribing — the value is in keeping up with THAT list, not an engagement feed. It reads subscriptions.list with read-only OAuth and never posts or changes anything on YouTube. Uploads are read from each channel's uploads playlist (playlistItems.list = 1 quota unit) rather than search.list (100 units), so two daily sweeps of 800+ channels use ~600 of the 10,000 free units/day. Dead/terminated playlists are detected and retired so they aren't retried forever.

descriptions.title: No LLM inside TubeScout — everything routes through NEXUS
descriptions.body: TubeScout deliberately hosts no model. Every news-card summary, every implement-worthiness score, and the Discover reasoning all go to NEXUS POST /synthesize with a pinned provider list (summaries: Groq→Cloudflare→Gemini; Discover: Groq default, gemma4 local switchable). This keeps per-video cost at effectively zero (NEXUS favours free/local models) and means TubeScout inherits NEXUS's failover for free. When NEXUS is unreachable the summarizer falls back to a trimmed description so the page never empties; a scorer simply leaves the video pending for the next run.

descriptions.title: Graceful degradation is the architecture
descriptions.body: The twice-daily cycle (sweep → reclassify → transcripts → summarize → dedup → score → scout) wraps every stage in a _safe() guard so one failure never aborts the rest. Summaries are decoupled from transcripts: the page uses the transcript when present, otherwise the description, so it keeps working even when YouTube IP-blocks the caption scraper. That scraper distinguishes 'no captions available' (skip quietly) from 'YouTube is blocking us' (raise IPBlocked) and, on a block, persists a multi-hour cooldown in the state table so it never extends the block by hammering.

descriptions.title: Two-pass channel classification
descriptions.body: Channels are bucketed into topics twice. The keyword organizer (organizer.classify) does whole-word matching (word-boundary regex, so 'ai' doesn't match 'painting') over title+description against the config topic map — strong on the specific tech buckets. The smart reclassifier (reclassify.py) then adds YouTube's own topicDetails.topicCategories and picks the most specific candidate via a TOPIC_RANK table (ai_ml/software_dev=10 down to lifestyle=1), so a [Lifestyle, Science] channel lands in science. This combination cut the 'other' pile from ~450 channels to ~3. User-set topics (topic_manual=1) are never overwritten.

descriptions.title: Conservative cross-channel dedup
descriptions.body: The same story often hits ten channels at once. dedup.run_dedup tokenizes each headline (stopword-filtered, len>2), clusters by Jaccard similarity ≥ dedup.threshold (0.55) within a dedup.window_hours (72h) window, and marks one canonical card with dup_of/dup_count on the rest. It is deliberately conservative — a false merge (hiding a distinct story) is worse than a miss — so the threshold is high and bounded by time. The page hides duplicates by default and shows '+N also covered' on the canonical card; ?show=all reveals them all.

descriptions.title: Privacy-preserving discovery
descriptions.body: The Discover recommender never feeds your taste into YouTube's recommendation or ad system. build_profile assembles a taste profile entirely on-machine (favorited channels, must-reads, AI/tech channels, your top implement-score tags) and a NEXUS provider reasons over it to suggest real channels — the reasoner can be switched to a fully-local gemma model in Settings so nothing leaves the machine at all. YouTube is touched only for a neutral search().list name→channel lookup that reveals nothing about you, and 'Follow privately' ingests a channel into TubeScout without subscribing on YouTube.

descriptions.title: Public page, owner controls, permanent link
descriptions.body: Reads (news, favorites, digest, settings views) are public; mutations are guarded centrally by the require_token_for_writes middleware, which enforces TUBESCOUT_PAGE_TOKEN on every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE when the token is set (open in local single-user mode). The page is served by the QI_TubeScout NSSM service (AppDirectory C:\APPS\TUBESCOUT, corrected 2026-06-18) and exposed by QI_TubeScoutTunnel as a permanent named Cloudflare tunnel at tubescout.quiddityinnovations.com — no open inbound port on the machine. The 'pairs with NEXUS' link auto-resolves to NEXUS's local or tunnel URL depending on how TubeScout itself is being viewed.
